ibrahim.name: Ibrahim Aboud
ibrahim.bio: Born in the old stone quarter of Ramallah, Ibrahim learned carpentry from his father and opened his own workshop at twenty. He built the family's first stone house with his own hands and led the family through four turbulent decades — every dispute in the family ended at his workbench, over cardamom coffee.

timeline.title: Born in the old quarter
timeline.text: Eldest of five children of a carpenter family in Ramallah.

timeline.title: Opens his workshop
timeline.text: Took over the family carpentry workshop on Al-Zahra Street.

timeline.title: Marries Fatima
timeline.text: A courtyard wedding the family still retells today.

timeline.title: Builds the stone house
timeline.text: Raised the family home on the southern hillside, stone by stone.

timeline.title: Passes the torch
timeline.text: Formally handed the workshop to Omar and Yousef.

timeline.title: Passes away
timeline.text: Buried beside the olive grove he planted in 1968.

photos: The first workshop on Al-Zahra Street, 1965

fatima.name: Fatima Aboud
fatima.bio: A weaver by craft and the family's gravitational center, Fatima kept the ledger of births, marriages and reconciliations for sixty years. Her notebooks remain the family's only written archive before 1980.

timeline.title: Born in Beitunia
timeline.text: Daughter of a weaving family from the hills.

timeline.title: Marries Ibrahim
timeline.text: Moved into the stone quarter of Ramallah.

timeline.title: The Sunday table
timeline.text: Founded the family tradition of Sunday lunch — never canceled since.

timeline.title: The first register
timeline.text: Compiled the hand-written family register of 120 years.

timeline.title: Going digital
timeline.text: Digitized her register with her granddaughter Rana.

omar.name: Omar Ibrahim Aboud
omar.bio: An engineer by training and the guardian of the family property, Omar splits his year between Amman and the old house in Ramallah. He keeps Ibrahim's workbench exactly where it stood.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: First child of Ibrahim and Fatima.

timeline.title: Engineering degree
timeline.text: Civil engineering, University of Jordan.

timeline.title: Marries Layla
timeline.text: Settled in Amman but returned every summer.

timeline.title: Restores the stone house
timeline.text: Led the two-year restoration of the family home.

photos: With Layla on the Jordan Trail, 2015

layla.name: Layla Nasser
layla.bio: For thirty years a principal in Amman, Layla taught four of the Aboud grandchildren to read before any school did. The family calls her 'the teacher' — a title she never refuses.

huda.name: Huda Ibrahim Aboud
huda.bio: The family's first physician, Huda built the pediatric clinic that still serves the western neighborhoods of Ramallah. She is remembered every spring when the clinic plants its anniversary olive tree.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: Second child of Ibrahim and Fatima.

timeline.title: Medical degree
timeline.text: Graduated medicine; chose pediatrics over surgery.

timeline.title: Opens the clinic
timeline.text: Founded the Aboud Children's Clinic with Karim's blueprints.

timeline.title: Passes away
timeline.text: Remembered by the clinic and the families it healed.

karim.name: Karim Haddad
karim.bio: Architect who drew the extension of the stone house — and, more quietly, half of modern Ramallah. Keeps a sketch of Huda's clinic framed above his desk.

ahmad.name: Ahmad Ibrahim Aboud
ahmad.bio: Crossed to Michigan in 1992 with two suitcases and his grandfather's spice tin. His restaurant became the Dearborn gathering point for the diaspora side of the family — every July the family flies in for Ahmad's open table.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: Third child of Ibrahim and Fatima.

timeline.title: Arrives in Michigan
timeline.text: Started as a line cook in a Dearborn diner.

timeline.title: Opens the restaurant
timeline.text: 'Cedar & Cardamom' — Ramallah recipes, Michigan portions.

timeline.title: Marries Mona
timeline.text: Met at a pharmacy conference in Detroit.

mona.name: Mona Saleh
mona.bio: Runs the pharmacy across from the restaurant — 'ahmad feeds them, I fix them' she says. Catalogs the family recipes allergen-free.

dalia.name: Dalia Ibrahim Aboud
dalia.bio: Fourth child and the family's lawyer — for land, for papers, for the ones who cannot pay. Trained the next generation of clerks in the family's attic office.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: Youngest daughter of Ibrahim and Fatima.

timeline.title: The attic office
timeline.text: Opened her practice above the old workshop.

timeline.title: Sister's oath
timeline.text: Finished Huda's clinic endowment after her passing.

fadi.name: Fadi Barakat
fadi.bio: Investigative journalist, radio voice, and the family's unofficial archivist. His tapes of Sunday lunches are how the grandchildren know their grandfathers.

yousef-sr.name: Yousef Ibrahim Aboud
yousef-sr.bio: The youngest son left for Beirut to photograph what words miss. Forty years of negatives — olive harvests, weddings, departures — sit in Beirut and Ramallah in equal halves.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: Youngest of Ibrahim and Fatima's six children.

timeline.title: First camera
timeline.text: Traded a winter coat for a second-hand camera.

timeline.title: 'Hillside' exhibition
timeline.text: Photographs of the family orchard shown in Beirut and Amman.

timeline.title: The last portrait
timeline.text: Photographed his father one week before his passing.

nour.name: Nour Khalil
nour.bio: Weaves Fatima's terrace patterns into modern textiles; the family shop in Beirut is half gallery, half living room.

salma.name: Salma Ibrahim Aboud
salma.bio: Youngest of the six, a pediatric nurse in Nablus, and the one who decided the family garden needed fig trees. Sundays, she drives the mountain road home without fail.

rana.name: Rana Omar Aboud
rana.bio: The engineer of the third generation — she digitized Fatima's register and built the first version of this family tree. Insists the data is 'just another kind of weaving'.

timeline.title: Born in Amman
timeline.text: First grandchild on the Omar branch.

timeline.title: Moves to Berlin
timeline.text: Joined a maps team; finds family addresses in her sleep.

timeline.title: The digital register
timeline.text: Sat with Fatima for a winter converting notebooks to bytes.

photos: With Fatima and the notebooks, winter 2018

tomas.name: Tomas Weber
tomas.bio: Berlin-born, speaks Arabic at Sunday video-calls with a Swabian accent the grandparents find delightful. Learned to make taboon bread on the first try.

sami.name: Sami Omar Aboud
sami.bio: Trained in Beirut, settled in Amman; his hummus has opinions. Runs a supper club where the family recipe for knafeh is officially 'closed source'.

aziza.name: Aziza Mansour
aziza.bio: Patisserie-trained in Paris; her ka'ek won a medal the family refuses to let her be modest about.

tariq.name: Tariq Omar Aboud
tariq.bio: Studies architecture in Amman and rehearses Karim's old stationery arguments about load-bearing stone. Sketches the stone house from every angle for a graduation project.

farah.name: Farah Haddad
farah.bio: Huda and Karim's daughter, carrying the studio's drafting tradition to Toronto. Her pavilion design for the clinic anniversary won the family's quietest standing ovation.

timeline.title: Born in Ramallah
timeline.text: First child of Huda and Karim.

timeline.title: The pavilion
timeline.text: Designed the clinic's 25th-anniversary pavilion in tribute.

timeline.title: Moves to Toronto
timeline.text: Opened a small studio focused on public spaces.

daniel.name: Daniel Kowalski
daniel.bio: The other half of every Farah project — married into the family and into the structural review process. Favorite uncle status: contested.

yousef-haddad.name: Yousef Haddad
yousef-haddad.bio: Named for his Beirut uncle and determined to rival Rana's spreadsheets. Works in London; sails on weekends; calls every eclipse without fail.

zayd.name: Zayd Ahmad Aboud
zayd.bio: Builds indie games in Dearborn and secretly beta-tested this interface. His current project: a puzzle game about an olive harvest.

maya.name: Maya Ahmad Aboud
maya.bio: Medical student in Ann Arbor, following aunt Huda's clinic stories like a compass. Her white coat photo is now an emoji in the family group chat.

noor.name: Noor Barakat
noor.bio: Fadi and Dalia's daughter — inherited the tape recorder, not the patience. Reports from London and co-edits the family's yearly newsletter.

hazem.name: Hazem Shaheen
hazem.bio: Motion designer who animated old family photos into a living archive for Yousef's 70th-birthday exhibition.

adam-barakat.name: Adam Barakat
adam-barakat.bio: Adam plays at the Ramallah academy and firmly believes a family reunion is eleven-a-side. Goal celebration: pointing at grandpa Fadi's press badge.

lina.name: Lina Yousef Aboud
lina.bio: Illustrates the family's Sunday-lunch comics; her panel of Fatima's register desk is already framed in the Beirut studio.

jad.name: Jad Yousef Aboud
jad.bio: Beats great-uncles at chess and won't tell them how. Keeps a ratings notebook; bribes accepted in knafeh.

mariam.name: Mariam Yousef Aboud
mariam.bio: The family's youngest explorer — climbed the stone house fig tree first and alphabetized Fatima's register second.

yara.name: Yara Weber
yara.bio: Fourth-generation Berliner who says 'tayta' before 'Oma' — inherited the dawn-person gene from Fatima.

nael.name: Nael Weber
nael.bio: Drum prodigy (pots and pans division). Already asks Sami for the knafeh recipe; gets the family shrug.

dana.name: Dana Mansour
dana.bio: Draws the family a new portrait every visit; they are taped inside the Amman kitchen cabinet.

rami.name: Rami Mansour
rami.bio: Named for his great-grandfather's workshop; his first word was reportedly 'hummus'.

elia.name: Elia Kowalski
elia.bio: Toronto's loudest four-year-old; insists his name means 'tallest' and the family's photos agree.

sofia.name: Sofia Kowalski
sofia.bio: The newest Toronto Aboud — born during a power outage, lit by candles and the family video-call.

waseem.name: Waseem Shaheen
waseem.bio: London branch, fourth generation — sleeps through Sunday video-calls with impressive commitment.

hala.name: Hala Shaheen
hala.bio: The family's newest member — great-grandmother Fatima's register now runs to four generations.
